newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr may need pullback before taking off.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr may need pullback before taking off.

text.p: Bulls and bears agreed, the dollar is headed higher.
What they can't agree about is whether the dollar has enough stamina left to attack key resistance levels right away or whether it first needs a consolidative pullback.
The dollar's action on Friday justified the quandary.
Dollar/mark briefly conquered 1.80 resistance, only to test the downside, a hair shy of strong support at 1.7850.
Dollar/yen mirrored that performance, stopping short of 116.40 but never in real danger of violating 115.25 support, a key level on a rising trendline from July 11.

Jim Chorek, director of currency research at Elliott Wave International, noted dollar/mark "has been in an equilbrium here for the past few days, chopping around the 1.79 area," after setting a fresh 71-month high on July 15.

"If we break dollar/mark support in the 1.7830/50 area, we are starting to look at 1.7650. I still think the long-term trend is up, but we'll need to see 1.7650 for the bull trend to resume," Cholek forecast.
Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy, viewed the dollar/mark's failure to take out 1.80 resistance as a reflexion of position-squaring ahead of the weekend.

"As long as we keep 1.7850 support, it's still bullish for dollar/mark," added Autotte who predicted "dollar/mark will be back above 1.80 next week and test 1.8040 (the 71-month high), and then, 1.8250, because there is nothing major in between."

Chartists said dollar/Swiss was giving some signs of weakness after setting a triple top this week at 1.4850. A pullback to 1.4650 cannot be ruled out and would support the scenario for a dollar/mark consolidation lower.
The outlook for dollar/yen is somewhat brighter and would be fostered by a close above 115.00, said Auttote who anticipated a near-term attack on 117.00 key resistance.
The 117.00 level is the recent dollar/yen high set on May 28 and the 38-percent retracement of the year's high/low move from 127.46 on May 1 to 110.62 on June 11.
Chorek pointed out that 117.00 also is a "key Elliott Wave resistance, the top of the previous B wave. A push above would send strong signals and we'll be looking at the 121.00 area."
Meanwhile, mark/yen retained some momentum from the impulsive reversal from the fall to a cycle low at 63.40 on July 14, indicating that 65.00/25 still are in the cards.
Sterling/mark failed to hold above 3.00, confirming some weakness already evident in cable.
